name: microstructure_volume_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Sudden volume spikes (> 5x 20-bar avg) without proportional price movement (< 0.15% move on the spike bar) indicate institutional accumulation/distribution. The price tends to move in the direction of the volume bar's close relative to its open in the next 10-20 bars. The inefficiency exists because institutional block trades absorb supply/demand without moving price, but the imbalance resolves once the block is fully absorbed. Hard to exploit manually because it requires real-time volume monitoring across 30+ stocks simultaneously.

entry.entry_price: market on bar after volume spike

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min (opening volume is naturally spiky)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (volume spikes are noise)
other_filters: skip if the spike bar range > 0.15% — that's a genuine move, not absorption

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — microstructure signal; institutional block trading practices are slow to change

weaknesses: 5x volume spike on 1-min can be a single large retail order, not institutional — false positives
Tight target (0.3%) and stop (0.25%) means costs eat a large % of edge — very sensitive to slippage
Low frequency — 5x spikes with small range are rare, may go days without a signal
prior_art: Volume spike absorption — institutional microstructure concept; not widely systematized
notes: Consider adding bid-ask imbalance data if available from Zerodha Kite API for better confirmation.
